text:
Alice K: heads-up — we need a decision on fragmentation policy for embeddings before next release. mixed-dim clients are hitting 413s and runtime split logic is messy.
Ben R: aggro problem. current splitter only looks at bytes, not dims, so we sometimes break a 1x1024 into weird fragments.
Claire S: proposal: add X-Embed-Shape header that gives (n,dim) pairs and X-Embed-Frag: policy=(auto|prefer-dims|prefer-bytes). runtime uses policy to pick split axis.
Maya P: console UX ask: show an "Estimated split & cost" preview on the request details panel. users should see how many fragments we'll create and expected units.
Raj V: quota model question — if we split server-side, do we charge per-fragment or per-original-request? this impacts tenant billing and fairshare.
Alice K: we bill per-token-equivalent (roughly per-vector) — but we can expose both metrics. backend: charge based on total processed vectors; console: show both "original" and "processed" units.
Ben R: runtime note: prefer-dims for mixed batches avoids tiny fragments that blow up batch density. but it's more expensive to compute handshake in ingress.
Claire S: tradeoff: ingress-aware splitting (early) vs runtime-split (late). early = simpler telemetry + console accuracy. late = less client churn.
Maya P: UX rollout: start with console-only preview + opt-in header. show tooltip: "Alpha: enable X-Embed-Frag to opt-in server-side fragmentation." then flip default after 2 weeks of canary.
infra-oncall: watchlist — if prefer-dims enables more small fragments, we'll see queueing in scheduler and P99 latency spikes. add a wiggle to autoscaler.
Ben R: telemetry plan: sample 5% of requests fully (pre+post split) and emit metric embed.split.count, embed.split.axis, embed.split.policy, embed.avg.dim, embed.fragments.per.request.
Claire S: also add a histogram for fragment sizes by dim so we can tune prefer-dims thresholds.
Maya P: console card layout: top line: "Estimated fragments: 3 — expected units: 2.1k" then a small breakdown by axis and cost. clickable "Why?" opens explainer.
Raj V: rollout steps: 1) SDK support for X-Embed-Shape (patch) + docs, 2) server-side opt-in header X-Embed-Frag=prefer-dims canary @10%, 3) telemetry flags + dashboard widget, 4) flip default @3 weeks if metrics stable.
Alice K: canary metric SLOs: fragment.rate < 1.2x baseline, queue-p99 < +30ms, error-rate < 0.1%. if any breach — rollback and investigate.
infra-oncall: canary alert to #eng-oncall + page if queue-p99 > threshold.
Ben R: quick example for SDK folks:
```bash
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer ..." \ 
     -H "X-Embed-Shape: count=2;dims=512,768" \ 
     -H "X-Embed-Frag: policy=prefer-dims" \ 
     -d '{"input":["a","b"]}' https://api.redwood/infer/embeddings
```
Claire S: tiny nit — shape header format: use CSV-ish so we can extend: e.g. "shapes=2:512,1:768" (count:dim pairs).
Maya P: I'll mock console card and tooltip copy. putting a draft in the docs repo and linking from the console CTA.
Raj V: billing note: add a billing flag `processed_vector_units` to usage events so finance can map to invoices.
deploy-bot: canary deployment started for embed-splitter v3 -> traffic=10% (flags: X-Embed-Frag=opt-in).
Ben R: dev test run shows fragment histograms emitted. uploading sample dashboard JSON to /dashboards/frag-policy.json.
infra-oncall: saw a small bump in scheduler queue depth at 10% — within threshold. continuing watch.
Alice K: action items: Claire implement header parsing + runtime branch, Ben wire telemetry + metrics, Maya mock console -> handoff to docs, Raj add billing event, infra-oncall add canary alerts.
Maya P: will add CTA text: "Preview how requests will be split and billed — enable fragment preview".
Raj V: FYI: finance wants 1 week notice before default flip.
Claire S: ok — will send PR and assign reviewers.
Ben R: thumbs-up on plan. :thumbsup:
Alice K: thanks — tagging follow-ups in Asana. ping me if you need quota wording.
deploy-bot: canary status: healthy -> monitoring for 24h.
infra-oncall: posting daily check-ins to #eng-platform-canaries for the next 48h.
Alice K: perfect — closing thread for now.
